dedupe_keys.name: daily psychiatric hospital admissions and ambient temperature in yazd iran 2014 to 2020 time series

description: This time series links daily admissions to the only psychiatric hospital in Yazd, a hot and arid city in central Iran, with ambient temperature. It was deposited on figshare in August 2025 by Saeed Fallah-Aliabadi, Mahnaz Sanaeefar, Mohammad Reza Khajehaminian, Hossein Fallahzadeh and Jun Yang to support their study of extreme temperatures and mental health admissions. The data cover 7,639 admissions from 2014 to 2020; the study examined daily minimum temperature with lags of up to a week and found that extreme heat raised admissions, especially for mood disorders, with stronger effects in men, married people and younger adults, while women and older adults responded later to extreme cold. The files, about 2.6 MB, are free to download under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Coverage is one city and one hospital. Caveats: the metadata do not list the variables or say how patient records were anonymised, and a single hospital limits generalisation. Simulation uses: temperature-dependent demand for inpatient mental health services, to test heat-related surge assumptions in hospital capacity models for arid cities. Related records: the England extreme heat hospital admissions study (case_study-england-extreme-heat-hospital-admissions) and the Portugal heatwave admissions study (case_study-portugal-heatwaves-hospital-admissions) look at heat and admissions elsewhere.
